players.product: Lithium niobate (LN) optical modulators for optical communications, incl. next-generation LN modulator (CDM) and ultra-high-speed optical modulation sub-assemblies

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 (year to March 2027) forecast (results and medium-term plan briefing): net sales JPY 2,345 hundred million on higher electrostatic chuck (ESC) volume in High-Performance Products; operating profit JPY 150 hundred million (FY2025: JPY 136 hundred million), with Cement down JPY 5 hundred million to JPY 50 hundred million and High-Performance Products up JPY 18 hundred million to JPY 42 hundred million; net income JPY 100 hundred million; assumptions JPY 155/USD and coal CIF US$140/t. Domestic cement demand is assumed at 3,000 ten-thousand t (FY2025: 3,053 ten-thousand t), own domestic sales 679 ten-thousand t and exports 160 ten-thousand t. A company respondent said H1 coal is secured at about US$135/t and H2 assumed at US$145/t against a spot level of about US$155 CIF; a cement price increase is in its final stage of consideration and is not included in the medium-term plan.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 forecast: net sales JPY 2,345 hundred million; operating profit JPY 150 hundred million

quarterly_data.signal: Electrostatic chuck capacity (results briefing, company respondents): the new ESC manufacturing building at the Ichikawa plant was completed at the end of March; equipment is being relocated and robotics introduced, and the earliest customer-qualified shipments are now planned for June instead of July; utilization against demand is about 80% in H1 and capacity runs at nearly 100% from H2, as customers' inventories of the company's products have fallen and requests to increase output from H2 have risen sharply; customers keep asking for more capacity, so machinery of several hundred million yen will be added in Q4, and the building has room for roughly 20% or more additional machines.
quarterly_data.figure: about 80% utilization in H1, about 100% from H2; building room for 20% or more machines

quarterly_data.signal: ESC demand and products (results briefing, company respondents): customers' forecasts for H2 are very strong and the FY2026 plan was set somewhat conservatively, with month-end forecasts possibly higher; demand is expected to keep growing next year and beyond because generative AI growth has left the needed chips in short supply, a shortage the company expects to continue through 2027 and 2028. Its ESCs are mainly for etching equipment; it aims to expand into other processes (deposition, cleaning, bonding, inspection, lithography), with the medium-term plan including more sales of mini heaters for bonding to multiple companies and dicing / inspection products - slightly under 10% of sales outside etching; logic accounts for only about 1 to 2 percent of units. A respondent said peers A and B are ahead in yield and cost structure, and that machinery capex will increase in 2027 and 2028 for automation and new production methods.
quarterly_data.figure: logic about 1 to 2 percent of ESC units; non-etching slightly under 10%

quarterly_data.signal: Optical and LN products (results briefing): a company respondent said High-Performance Products operating profit is planned to rise JPY 46 hundred million over the medium-term plan, mainly on ESC volume; optical products add a combined JPY 4 hundred million - a Hamamatsu subsidiary that makes optical products (lasers for semiconductor processing and final-inspection equipment) on contract for semiconductor manufacturing equipment, which raised production from April at customers' request and aims for about 1.3 times during the plan, plus the effect of rationalizing the LN modulator business.
quarterly_data.figure: High-Performance Products +JPY 46 hundred million; optical products +JPY 4 hundred million; about 1.3 times

quarterly_data.signal: Cement strategy (results briefing): the president said under-target results in the previous plan reflected weaker-than-expected cement demand, cost increases and a weak semiconductor market. Company respondents said the plan's JPY 65 hundred million cement profit increase relies on the effects of past carbon-neutral investment (less coal use), higher recycling-processing fees, cheaper coal grades and petroleum coke, exports, an Australian downstream strategy and a planned business in the Philippines; manufacturing cost reductions of JPY 63 hundred million by FY2028 versus FY2025 comprise about JPY 40 hundred million from recycling and carbon-neutral investment and JPY 20 hundred million or more from logistics and sales efficiency. Coal procurement has not been disrupted by the Middle East situation and naphtha-derived materials are secured, though prices are rising; capex of about JPY 1,000 hundred million is planned over the plan.
quarterly_data.figure: cement profit +JPY 65 hundred million plan; cost reductions JPY 63 hundred million; capex about JPY 1,000 hundred million
